title: Machine-learning model reduces misdiagnosis of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
summary: A prospective cohort of 1,393 patients with suspected HIT from 10 centers (119 confirmed by the HIPA reference assay) was used to train models on six predictors, with a 25% validation set. AUROC was 0.99 (95% CI 0.97-1.00) for all models, and false negatives fell by 50.0%, 66.7% and 64.3% versus the recommended algorithm for ELISA, PaGIA and CLIA. Validation was a hold-out within one cohort, so wider validation is still needed.
ai_technology: Support vector machine and gradient boosting machine on clinical and immunoassay data
organization: University of Bern; University Hospital of Bern

evidence.tested: Models were compared against the 4Ts score plus immunoassay in a 25% hold-out set of a prospective cohort, with HIPA as reference.
evidence.unknown: Performance in other settings is unknown. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: SVM and gradient boosting models combined immunoassay results and clinical variables to diagnose HIT.
